items.statement: Only inversion and left concatenation, needed by Example 11.6.3, are curated. The right-concatenation and transport equivalences with their explicit inverses remain lower-priority exercise work.

The general equivalence criterion for maps into empty types is curated for Section 11.5. The displayed product/coproduct unit, absorption, commutativity, associativity, and distributivity equivalences themselves still need formalization; that auxiliary alone does not complete this example.

The triangle laws needed by Theorem 11.1.6 and the three equivalence implications are curated. Package the standalone assertions in parts (a) and (b), and prove the final consequence that any section or retraction of an equivalence is an equivalence. These remaining exercise results are deferred until section Agda is complete.
Show that the terminal map A → unit is an equivalence exactly when A is contractible. Only part (b), needed by Section 11.1, is currently curated.
Show that bounded quotient-and-remainder decompositions of a natural number are unique: if a = qb + r and a = q'b + r', with both remainders less than nonzero b, then q = q' and r = r'.
Prove the alternative characterization of prime natural numbers stated in Exercise 8.5.
Prove the decidable-equality part of Exercise 8.9 for dependent functions out of a finite type.
Define the greatest common divisor as the maximal element of the type of common divisors.
Show that there are infinitely many primes congruent to 3 modulo 4.
Show that the integers modulo a prime form a field.
Prove the backward direction of the adjointness equivalence for the cofibonacci sequence.
Establish the stated implications among decidable equality of a base, its fibers, and their dependent sum.
Show that a dependent product of decidable types indexed by Fin(k) is decidable.
Prove decidability of distances between multiples and construct Bézout coefficients for natural numbers.
Construct and prove uniqueness of prime factorizations of natural numbers.
Construct the cofibonacci sequence and prove the forward divisibility implication.
